newsitem.title: IRAQ: Bahraini businessmen in Iraq seeking trade.
newsitem.headline: Bahraini businessmen in Iraq seeking trade.

text.p: A group of Bahraini businessmen are visiting Iraq for the first time since the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait, seeking deals under an oil-for-food pact signed by Baghdad and the United Nations.

"We are here for business. We want to bring to Iraq foodstuffs and medicine allowed by the oil agreement with the United Nations," Abdul Ridha al-Kazrouni, one of the Bahraini businessmen, told Reuters on Wednesday.
He said they had met officials from the ministers of health, trade, transport and communications and industry to learn Iraq's needs of humanitarian goods.
"We are expecting them to deliver us lists of their needs later today," he said.

The oil deal Iraq signed with the United Nations in May allows Baghdad oil sales of $2 billion over six months to buy essentials for Iraqis, under stringent U.N. trade sanctions since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The pact, which is renewable, was about to be implemented in September when it was halted because Baghdad sent troops to intervene in Kurdish fighting in the north, an area closed to its forces since 1991.
Iraq gave the Bahraini businessmen a red-carpet welcome, with newspapers reporting their movement from one ministry to another to meet officials.

Iraq's relations with Arab Gulf states are strained since Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait in 1990. Bahrain and other Gulf allies fought alongside the U.S.-led multinational force which evicted Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991.
Oman and Qatar have since improved ties with Baghdad but others like Saudi Arabia and Kuwait reject direct dealings with Baghdad.
